exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise K, case 1: Kareem
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Kareem is 5 months old. He weighs 5.2 kg Length 69 cm. His axillary temperature is 37.5 C. His mother said he is not eating well. She said he feels hot, and she want a health worker to help him. Kareem is able to drink, has no vomiting, does not have convulsions, and is not lethargic or unconscious. Kareem has no cough or diarrhea. Because Kareem's temperature is 37.5o C and he feels hot, the health worker assessed Kareem further for signs related to fever. The mother said: Kareem’s fever began 2 days ago. He has not had measles within the last 3 months. He does not have stiff neck. When the health worker checked the result of Kareem's malaria test, he found it positive. And there are no genelized rash of measles.
learningPoints: Kareem has fever (37.5°C and feels hot), no general danger sign, no stiff neck, and a positive malaria test: MALARIA.
He has no generalized rash and no measles in the last 3 months: do not classify measles.
exercises.explain: Kareem has fever (37.5°C and feels hot), no general danger sign, no stiff neck, and a positive malaria test: MALARIA. He has no generalized rash and no measles in the last 3 months: do not classify measles.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise K, case 2: Rania
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Rania is 13-month-old. She weighs 9.4 kg Length 66.5 cm, Her temperature is 37o C. Her family brought her to the clinic because she feels hot and has had cough for 3 days. She is able to drink. She has not vomited or had convulsion, and is not lethargy unconscious.The health worker said, “I am going to check her cough now.” Said the health worker counted 51 breaths per minute. There was no chest indrawing, no stridor and no wheeze when Rania was calm. Rania did not have diarrhea.“Now, I will check her fever,” said the health worker. Her mother said, “Rania has felt hot off and on for 2 days.” She has not had measles within the last 3 months. She does not have stiff neck. When the health worker checked the result of Rania’s malaria test, he found it positive. Rania has no generalized rash.. Her eyes are red. She has mouth ulcers. They are not deep and extensive. She does not have pus draining from the eye. She does not have clouding of the cornea. Recorded the child’s signs and classify them on the Recording Form.
learningPoints: Rania is 13 months old: fast breathing is 40 or more. She has 51: PNEUMONIA.
Fever with a positive malaria test and no danger sign or stiff neck: MALARIA.
She has no generalized rash and has not had measles in the last 3 months: do not classify measles, even though she has mouth ulcers.
exercises.explain: Rania is 13 months old: fast breathing is 40 or more. She has 51: PNEUMONIA. Fever with a positive malaria test and no danger sign or stiff neck: MALARIA. She has no generalized rash and has not had measles in the last 3 months: do not classify measles, even though she has mouth ulcers.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise K, case 3: Manal
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Manal is 12-month-old. She is weight 7.2 kg Length 52cm. Her axillary temperature is 36.5 o C. Her mother brought Manal to the health center today because she feels hot. Manal has no general danger signs. She does not have cough or difficult breathing. When asked about Diarrhea, the mother said, “Yes Manal has had diarrhea for 2 to 3 days.” She has not seen any blood in the stool. Manal has not been lethargic or unconscious. Her eyes are not sunken. She drinks normally. Her skin pinch returns immediately. The health worker said, “You brought Manal today because she feels hot. I will check her for fever. Her mother said that Manal has felt hot for 2 days. She had no measles within the last three months. There is no stiff neck. When the health worker checked the result of Manal’s malaria test, he found it negative. In addition, no generalized rash, she has no other cause of fever.
learningPoints: Manal has no signs of dehydration: NO DEHYDRATION.
She has a history of fever (felt hot for 2 days) and a negative malaria test: FEVER NO MALARIA.
exercises.explain: Manal has no signs of dehydration: NO DEHYDRATION. She has a history of fever (felt hot for 2 days) and a negative malaria test: FEVER NO MALARIA.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise K, case 4: Duria
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Duria is 3 years old. She weighs 10 kg. Height 73 cm, her axillary temperature is 38 o C. Her mother brought her to the health center because she has a cough. She also has a rash. The health worker checked Duria for general danger signs. She was able to drink, she had not been vomiting everything, and she did not have convulsions. She was not lethargic or unconscious. The health worker assessed Duria’s cough. The mother told the health worker, Duria had been coughing for 2 days. The health worker counted 42 breaths per minute. The health worker did not see chest indrawing. He did not hear stridor or wheeze when Duria was calm. When the health worker asked if Duria had diarrhea, the mother said, “No.”Next, the health worker assessed Duria’s fever. She has felt hot for 2 days, the mother said. She does not have stiff neck. She When the health worker checked the result of Duria’s malaria test, he found it positive. Duria has a generalized rash. She does not have mouth ulcers. Pus is not draining from the eye. There is no clouding of cornea.
learningPoints: Duria is 3 years old: fast breathing is 40 or more. She has 42: PNEUMONIA.
Fever and a positive malaria test: MALARIA.
She has a generalized rash and no complications: MEASLES. (Classify measles in the question after this exercise.)
exercises.explain: Duria is 3 years old: fast breathing is 40 or more. She has 42: PNEUMONIA. Fever and a positive malaria test: MALARIA. She has a generalized rash and no complications: MEASLES. (Classify measles in the question after this exercise.)

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise L: fever (video)
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: In this exercise, you will watch a demonstration of how to assess and classify a child with fever. You will see examples of signs related to fever and measles. You will practice identifying stiff neck. Then you will watch a case study.

questions.question: Watch children 1 to 4 on the video. Does each child have a stiff neck?
points: Check your answer for each child with the answer on the video.
questions.explain: If the neck feels stiff and there is resistance to bending, the child has a stiff neck.

questions.question: The case study on the video: record the child's signs and classify the child's illness.
points: Check your Recording Form with the answer on the video.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise M, case 1: Hala
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Hala is 3 year old. She weighs 13 kg, her height is 70cm her temperature is 37.5 C. Her mother came to the clinic today because Hala has felt hot for the last 2 days. She was crying last night and complained that her ear is hurting.The health worker checked and found no general danger signs.Hala does not have cough or difficult breathing. She does not have diarrhea. Her fever was classified as MALARIA. Next, the health worker asked about Hala's ear problem. The mother said she is sure Hala has ear pain. The child cried most of the night because her ear hurt. There has been discharge coming from Hala's ear on and off for about a year, said the mother. The health worker did not see any pus draining from the child's ear. He felt behind the child's ears and felt tender swelling behind one ear. Record Hala's signs of ear problem and classify them on the Recording Form.
learningPoints: Hala has tender swelling behind one ear: MASTOIDITIS (pink row).
She also has ear pain and discharge on and off for about a year, but always select the more serious classification.
exercises.explain: Hala has tender swelling behind one ear: MASTOIDITIS (pink row). She also has ear pain and discharge on and off for about a year, but always select the more serious classification.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise M, case 2: Mona
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Mona is 18 months old. She weighs 9 kg. her length is 57cm her temperature is 37 C. Her mother said that Mona had discharge coming from her ear for the last 3 days.Mona does not have any general danger signs. She does not have cough or difficult breathing. She does not have diarrhea and she does not have fever. The health worker asked about Mona's ear problem. The mother said that Mona does not have ear pain, but the discharge has been coming from the ear for 3 or 4 days. The health worker saw pus draining from the child's right ear. He did not feel any tender swelling behind either ear. Record 's signs Mona of ear problem and classify them on the Recording
learningPoints: Pus is seen draining from Mona's ear and the discharge has been present for 3 or 4 days, less than 14 days: ACUTE EAR INFECTION.
exercises.explain: Pus is seen draining from Mona's ear and the discharge has been present for 3 or 4 days, less than 14 days: ACUTE EAR INFECTION.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise N: palmar pallor and oedema (photographs)
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise O, case 1: Nadia
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Nadia is 18 months old. She weighs 8 kg length 96 cm. Her temperature is 38.5 C. Her mother brought her today because the child has felt hot and has a rash. The health worker saw that Nadia looks like skin and bones. The health worker checked for general danger signs. Nadia is able to drink, has not vomited, has not had convulsions, is not convulsing now and is not lethargic orunconscious. She does not have cough or difficult breathing. She does not have diarrhea. Because Nadia's mother said the child felt hot, and because her temperature is 38.5 C, the health worker assessed her for fever. Nadia lives where there is high malaria risk. She has had fever for 5 days. Her rash is generalized rash, and she has red eyes. She has measles. She does not have a stiff neck. The health worker assessed her for signs of measles complications. Nadia does not have mouth ulcers. There is no pus draining from the eye and no clouding of the cornea. Nadia does not have an ear problem. The health worker next checked her for malnutrition or anemia. She does not have edema of both feet. The health worker determined her weight for length. (Look at the weight for length chart in your chart booklet.) , health worker check MUAC and found it 11 cm. Since Nadia did not have medical complications then the health worker offer her an appetite test, after 30 minute the health worker found that Nadia finished more than the amount offer for her, and decide that Nadia passed the appetite test. Then checked for anemia and found no palmar pallor.
learningPoints: Nadia has no general danger sign, no stiff neck, and lives in a high malaria risk area. The book does not give a malaria test result: do the malaria test before you classify her fever (the facilitator guide's answer is MALARIA).
She has a generalized rash and no complications: MEASLES.
MUAC 11 cm (less than 115 mm), no oedema, no medical complication, and she passed the appetite test: UNCOMPLICATED SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRITION.
No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.
exercises.explain: Nadia has no general danger sign, no stiff neck, and lives in a high malaria risk area. The book does not give a malaria test result: do the malaria test before you classify her fever (the facilitator guide's answer is MALARIA). She has a generalized rash and no complications: MEASLES. MUAC 11 cm (less than 115 mm), no oedema, no medical complication, and she passed the appetite test: UNCOMPLICATED SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRITION. No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise O, case 2: Idris
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Idris is 11 months old. He weighs 8 kg. Length= 08 cm, His temperature is 37 C. His mother says he has had a dry cough for the last 3 weeks.Idris does not have any general danger sign. The health worker assessed his cough. It has been present for 21 days. He counted 41 breaths per minute. The health worker does not see chest indrawing. There is no stridor when the child is calm and there is no wheeze. Idris does not have diarrhea. He has not had a fever during this illness. He does not have an ear problem. The health worker checked Idris for malnutrition. There is no oedema of both feet. MUAC 11 cm Since Idris did not have medical complications then the health worker offer her an appetite test, he give the mother 92 g of ready to use therapeutic food and asked the mother to feed Idris, after 30 minute the health worker found that Idris could not finished even third than the amount offer for him, and decide that Idris did not passed the appetite test. Then checked for anemia found His palms are very pale and appear almost white.
learningPoints: Idris is 11 months old: fast breathing is 50 or more. He has 41, no chest indrawing and no stridor: COUGH OR COLD. He has coughed for 21 days, more than 2 weeks: a chronic cough.
MUAC 11 cm and he did not finish the RUTF: COMPLICATED SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRITION.
His palms are very pale and appear almost white: SEVERE ANAEMIA.
exercises.explain: Idris is 11 months old: fast breathing is 50 or more. He has 41, no chest indrawing and no stridor: COUGH OR COLD. He has coughed for 21 days, more than 2 weeks: a chronic cough. MUAC 11 cm and he did not finish the RUTF: COMPLICATED SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRITION. His palms are very pale and appear almost white: SEVERE ANAEMIA.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise O, case 3: Gaafar
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Gaafar is 9 months old. He weighs 0 kg. Length 67 cm His temperature is 36.8 C.. He is at the clinic today because his mother and father are concerned about his diarrhea. He does not have any general danger signs. He does not have cough or difficult breathing. He has had diarrhea for 5 days, the father said. They have not seen any blood in the stool. Gaafar is not restless or irritable. He is not lethargic or unconscious. His eyes are not sunken. He is thirsty and eager to drink water offered to him. His skin pinch goes back slowly. He does not have fever. He does not have an ear problem. Next, the health worker checked for signs of malnutrition and anemia. He does not have oedema of both feet. MUAC is 13 cm Gafar did not have medical complications then the health worker offer him an appetite test he give the mother 92 g of ready to use therapeutic food and asked the mother to feed Gafar, after 30 minute the health worker found that Gafar finished more than third of the amount offer for him, and decide that Gafar passed the appetite test. There is no palmar pallor.
learningPoints: Gaafar is thirsty and eager to drink, and his skin pinch goes back slowly: SOME DEHYDRATION.
MUAC 13 cm, no oedema: NO ACUTE MALNUTRITION (the book gives his weight as 0 kg, so weight for length cannot be checked).
No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.
exercises.explain: Gaafar is thirsty and eager to drink, and his skin pinch goes back slowly: SOME DEHYDRATION. MUAC 13 cm, no oedema: NO ACUTE MALNUTRITION (the book gives his weight as 0 kg, so weight for length cannot be checked). No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise O, case 4: Omran
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Omran is 37 months old. He weighs 9.5 kg length 90cm His temperature is 37.5 C. His mother says he feels hot. He has been crying and rubbing his ear. The health worker checks Omran for general danger signs. He is able to drink, does not vomit everything he drinks, has not had convulsions and is not lethargic or unconscious. He does not have cough or diarrhea. Because his mother has reported a history of fever and because his temperature is 37.5 C, the health worker assesses Omran for fever. The risk of malaria is high. He has had fever for 3 days, says his mother. He has not had measles in the last 3 months. His neck moves easily. There are no signs suggesting measles. The health worker asks if Omran has an ear problem. The mother says he has had ear pain. She also says she has seen ear discharge for about 5 days. The health worker sees pus draining from the ear. He does not feel any tender swelling behind either ear. He then checks the child for malnutrition and anemia. Omran looks thin;. He does not have oedema of both feet. MUAC 9.5 cm. Omran did not have medical complications then the health worker offer him an appetite test he give the mother 92 g of ready to use therapeutic food (RUFT) and asked the mother to feed Omran, after 30 minute the health worker found that Omran finished more than third of the amount offer for him, and decide that Omran passed the appetite test. He does not have palmar pallor.
learningPoints: The risk of malaria is high and Omran has no danger sign or stiff neck. The book gives no malaria test result: do the test before you classify his fever.
Ear pain, and pus draining from the ear for about 5 days: ACUTE EAR INFECTION.
MUAC 9.5 cm, no medical complication, passed the appetite test: UNCOMPLICATED SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRITION.
No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.
exercises.explain: The risk of malaria is high and Omran has no danger sign or stiff neck. The book gives no malaria test result: do the test before you classify his fever. Ear pain, and pus draining from the ear for about 5 days: ACUTE EAR INFECTION. MUAC 9.5 cm, no medical complication, passed the appetite test: UNCOMPLICATED SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRITION. No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise Q: immunization and vitamin A
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Part 1: Review the information in section 8.1 about contraindications to immunizations. Then decide if a contraindication is present for each of the following children:

questions.question: If the child will be treated at home with antibiotics
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization
questions.explain: There are no contraindications to immunization of a sick child if the child is well enough to go home.

questions.question: If the child has a local skin infection
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization

questions.question: If the child had convulsion immediately after Penta 1 and needs Penta 2 and OPV 2 today
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization
questions.explain: Give OPV 2 but do not give Penta 2: do not give Penta 2 or Penta 3 to a child who has had convulsions or shock within 3 days of the most recent dose.

questions.question: If the child has a chronic heart problem
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization

questions.question: If the child is being referred for severe classification
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization
questions.explain: If a child is going to be referred, do not immunize the child before referral.

questions.question: If the child is exclusively breastfed
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization

questions.question: If the child older brother had convulsion last year
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization

questions.question: If the child was jaundiced at birth
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization

questions.question: If the child is MODERATE ACUTE MALNUTRITION
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization
questions.explain: It is very important to immunize sick and malnourished children.

questions.question: If the child is known to have AIDS and has not received any immunizations at all
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization
questions.explain: Give OPV, Penta and measles, but do not give BCG to a child known to have AIDS.

questions.question: If the child has NO PNEUMONIA: COUGH OR COLD
options: Immunize this child today if due for immunization

questions.question: 1. Salim, 6 months old. No general danger signs. Classified as NO PNEUMONIA: COUGH OR COLD and NO ANAEMIA AND NO ACUTE MALNUTRITION. o Immunization history: BCG, OPV 0, OPV 1, OPV 2, Penta 1 and Penta 2, PCV1 and PCV2 Rota1 and Rota 2 given 6 weeks ago. o Is Salim up-to-date with his immunizations?   o What immunizations, if any, does Salim need?   o When should he return for his next immunization?   o Should he be given vitamin A today?
points: Not up to date.
He needs Penta 3, OPV 3 and IPV (facilitator guide). By the schedule he also needs PCV 3 and Rota 3.
He should return at 9 months of age for measles, yellow fever and Men A.
Yes, vitamin A today, because he is 6 months old.

questions.question: 2. Samia, 3 months old. No general danger signs. Classified as diarrhea with NO DEHYDRATION and also ANAEMIA. o Immunization history: BCG, OPV 0, OPV 1, Penta 1, PCV1 and Rota 1 were given 5 weeks ago. o Is Samia up-to-date with her immunizations?   o What immunizations, if any, does Samia need?   o Samia has diarrhea. What immunizations will she receive at her next visit?   o What advice should you give Samia’s mother according to immunization schedule you have in your clinic?   o When should she return for her next immunization?   o Should she be given Vitamin A today?
points: Not up to date.
She needs OPV 2, Penta 2, PCV 2 (and Rota 2). Do not count (record) OPV 2, because she has diarrhoea.
At her next visit: Penta 3, repeat OPV 2, and the other doses due.
Return in 4 weeks.
No vitamin A: she is 3 months old.

questions.question: 3. Ali, 9 months old. No general danger signs. Classified as PNEUMONIA, MALARIA, NO ANAEMIA AND NO ACUTE MALNUTRITION. o Immunization history: BCG, OPV 0, OPV1 PCV1 ROTA 1 and Penta 1.When Ali was 7 months old, he received OPV2, PCV2 ROTA2 Penta 2, and vitamin A supplement. o Is Ali up-to-date with his immunizations?   o What immunizations, if any, does Ali need?   o When should he return for his next immunizations?   o What advice should you give Ali’s mother according to Immunization schedule you have in your clinic?   o Should he be given vitamin A today?
points: Not up to date.
He needs Penta 3, OPV 3, IPV, PCV 3 and Measles (by the schedule also Rota 3, Yellow fever and Men A).
No vitamin A today: he received it at 7 months, less than 6 months ago. He returns for vitamin A when 6 months have passed.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise R, case 1: Omer
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Omer is 9 months old. He weighs 9.5 kg. Length 60cm, his temperature is 37.5 C. His mother says he has had diarrhea for 1 week. Omer does not have any general danger signs. He does not have cough or difficult breathing.The health worker assessed Omer for signs of diarrhea. The mother said earlier that Omer has had diarrhea for 1 week. Omer does not have blood in the stool. He is not restless or irritable; he is not lethargic or unconscious. He has sunken eyes. He is thirsty and drinks eagerly when offered a drink. His skin pinch goes back slowly. Next, the health worker assessed for additional signs related to fever. Omer 's mother says he has felt hot for about 2 days.,he has not had measles in the last 3 months. He does not have a stiff neck and he did not have signs suggesting measles.There is no ear problem. The health worker checked for signs of malnutrition he does not have edema of both feet. MUAC is 7226 The health worker determined his weight for length. Omer does not have palmar pallor2 Omer has had BCG, Penta 1, Penta 2, and Penta 3. He has also had OPV 0, OPV 1, OPV 2 and OPV 3 PCV 1 PCV 2 PCV3 and Rota1 and Rota2. Omer’s card has no record of previous vitamin A treatment or supplementation, and his mother does not recall his receiving any.
learningPoints: Sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, skin pinch goes back slowly: SOME DEHYDRATION. 7 days, no blood: no persistent diarrhoea, no dysentery.
He has had fever for 2 days and no danger sign or stiff neck: do the malaria test before you classify the fever (the book gives no result).
The book's MUAC (“7226”) and length (60 cm) cannot be right: measure again before you classify his nutritional status.
No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.
Immunization: he needs Measles, Yellow fever and Men A (and IPV and Rota 3 by the schedule). He needs vitamin A today.
exercises.explain: Sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, skin pinch goes back slowly: SOME DEHYDRATION. 7 days, no blood: no persistent diarrhoea, no dysentery. He has had fever for 2 days and no danger sign or stiff neck: do the malaria test before you classify the fever (the book gives no result). The book's MUAC (“7226”) and length (60 cm) cannot be right: measure again before you classify his nutritional status. No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA. Immunization: he needs Measles, Yellow fever and Men A (and IPV and Rota 3 by the schedule). He needs vitamin A today.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise R, case 2: Najwa
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Najwa is 4 months old. She weighs 5.5 kg. Her length is 60 cm, her temperature is 38.0 C.She is in the clinic today because she has diarrhea, she does not have any general danger signs. She is not coughing and does not have difficulty breathing. The health worker assessed her further for signs of diarrhea. She has had diarrhea for 2 days and there is blood in the stool, said the mother. Najwa was not restless or irritable; she was not unconscious or lethargic. Her eyes were not sunken. She drank normally, and did not seem to be thirsty. Her skin pinch went back immediately. The health worker next assessed her for fever. Najwa has had fever for 2 days, said the mother. She has not had measles in the last 3 months. She does not have a stiff neck. She has runny nose. There are no signs suggesting measles and malaria rapid diagnostic test was negative Najwa does not have an ear problem. The health worker checked her for sever acute malnutrition and anemia. She does not have oedema of both feet; the health worker determined her weight for height. Had no palmer pallor. At birth, Najwa received BCG and OPV 0. Four weeks ago, she received Penta 1 and OPV 1 PCV1 ROTA1.
learningPoints: No signs of dehydration: NO DEHYDRATION. Blood in the stool: DYSENTERY.
Fever with a negative malaria test: FEVER NO MALARIA.
Weight for length (5.5 kg, 60 cm, girl): -2 z-scores or more: NO ACUTE MALNUTRITION. She is 4 months old: MUAC is not used.
No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.
Immunization: she needs Penta 2, OPV 2, PCV 2 and Rota 2 today. No vitamin A: she is under 6 months.
exercises.explain: No signs of dehydration: NO DEHYDRATION. Blood in the stool: DYSENTERY. Fever with a negative malaria test: FEVER NO MALARIA. Weight for length (5.5 kg, 60 cm, girl): -2 z-scores or more: NO ACUTE MALNUTRITION. She is 4 months old: MUAC is not used. No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA. Immunization: she needs Penta 2, OPV 2, PCV 2 and Rota 2 today. No vitamin A: she is under 6 months.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise R, case 3: Jamila
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Jamila is 37 months old. She weighs 15.3 kg. height 80 cm, her temperature is 38.5 C. Jamila's family brought her to the clinic today because she has a stomachache, feels hot, has a runny nose andrash and she is coughing. The health worker checked her for general danger signs. She was able to drink, did not vomit everything she drank, did not have convulsions, and was not lethargic or unconscious. The health worker assessed the child for cough or difficult breathing. The parents said she has been coughing for 2 days. The health worker counted 55 breaths a minute. He did not see chest indrawing. He did not hear any unusual noise when she breathed in or out. Jamila does not have diarrhea, said the parents. However, she has been feeling hot, they said. The risk of malaria is high. She has had fever for two days. She has not had measles in the last 3 months. Her neck moves easily. The health worker looked for signs suggesting measles. Her rash was not generalized; it was only on her hand. Malaria test was positive. Jamila did not have an ear problem, said the parents. The health worker checked Jamila for malnutrition and anemia. She does not have edema of both feet. The health worker determined her weight for age. MUAC 13 cm. She does not have palmar pallor. Jamila has received BCG, OPV 0, OPV 1, OPV 2, OPV 3, Penta 1, Penta 2, and Penta 3 PCV1 PCV2 PCV3 and ROTA1 ROTA 2. Jamila has received vitamin A supplementation one month ago.
learningPoints: 37 months old with 55 breaths per minute: fast breathing, PNEUMONIA.
Fever and a positive malaria test: MALARIA. Her rash is only on her hand, not generalized: do not classify measles.
MUAC 13 cm: NO ACUTE MALNUTRITION. No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.
She is up to date for her age except measles, yellow fever and Men A, which the book's history does not list; she had vitamin A one month ago, so no vitamin A today.
exercises.explain: 37 months old with 55 breaths per minute: fast breathing, PNEUMONIA. Fever and a positive malaria test: MALARIA. Her rash is only on her hand, not generalized: do not classify measles. MUAC 13 cm: NO ACUTE MALNUTRITION. No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA. She is up to date for her age except measles, yellow fever and Men A, which the book's history does not list; she had vitamin A one month ago, so no vitamin A today.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Exercise R, case 4: Amel
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Assess and classify the sick child (2023)
narrative: Amel is 6 months old, weighs 4 kg, length 55 cm her temperature is 37 C, her mother brought her to the clinic because Amel has cough. Her mother is also concerned that Amel looks thin. The health worker did not find any general danger signs. Then he assessed her cough; The mother said Amel had cough for 4 days. The health worker counted 52 breaths per minute. Amel did not have chest indrawing, and there was no stridor and was no wheeze when the child was calm.Amel did not have diarrhea, and she did not have fever. There was no ear problem, said the mother. She did not have oedema of both feet. The health worker determined the child's weight for length. MUAC 12.4 cm. The health worker saw that Amel did not have palmar pallor. She has had BCG, OPV 0. She received OPV 1, and Penta 1,PCV1 ROTA1 four weeks ago. She has not had vitamin A.
learningPoints: 6 months old with 52 breaths per minute: fast breathing, PNEUMONIA.
MUAC 12.4 cm (124 mm), 115 up to 125 mm: MODERATE ACUTE MALNUTRITION.
No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA.
Immunization: she needs OPV 2, Penta 2, PCV 2 and Rota 2. Vitamin A: yes, she is 6 months old and has not had it.
exercises.explain: 6 months old with 52 breaths per minute: fast breathing, PNEUMONIA. MUAC 12.4 cm (124 mm), 115 up to 125 mm: MODERATE ACUTE MALNUTRITION. No palmar pallor: NO ANAEMIA. Immunization: she needs OPV 2, Penta 2, PCV 2 and Rota 2. Vitamin A: yes, she is 6 months old and has not had it.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Identify treatment, Exercise A: is urgent referral needed?
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Identify treatment (2023)
narrative: In this exercise you will decide whether or not urgent referral is needed. Tick the appropriate answer.

questions.question: 1. Neema is a 6-month-old girl. She has no general danger signs. She has: o COUGH OR COLD o DIARRHEA with NO DEHYDRATION o PERSISTENT DIARRHOEA o NO ACUTE SEVER MALNUTRTION o NO ANAEMIA Does Neema need an urgent referral? Yes ____ No____
questions.explain: No. Neema has no general danger signs and no severe classifications.

questions.question: 2. Daoud is a 7- month-old boy. He has no general danger signs. He has: o MASTOIDITIS o MALARIA o NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION o NO ANAEMIA Does Daoud need urgent referral? Yes ____ No ____
questions.explain: Yes. Daoud has a severe classification: MASTOIDITIS.

questions.question: 3. Maher is a 2- years -old boy. He had convulsions this morning and is not eating well. He has: o NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION o NO ANAEMIA Does Maher need urgent referral? Yes ____ No ____
questions.explain: Yes. Maher has a general danger sign: convulsions.

questions.question: 4. Habib is a 9-months -old boy. He is lethargic. He has: o Diarrhoea with SEVERE DEHYDRATION o NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION o NO ANAEMIA. The clinic can provide IV therapy Does Habib need urgent referral? Yes _____ No____
questions.explain: No. Habib's general danger sign may be related to dehydration, and his only severe classification is SEVERE DEHYDRATION. Since this clinic can give IV therapy, Habib should be given IV therapy at the clinic.

questions.question: 5. Ibrahim is a 15-month-old child. Ibrahim is not able to drink. He has: o Diarrhoea with SEVERE DEHYDRATION, o NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION, o NO ANEMIA The clinic cannot provide IV therapy nor NG therapy. Does Ibrahim need urgent referral? Yes _____ No ____
questions.explain: Yes. His only severe classification is SEVERE DEHYDRATION, so use Plan C. The clinic cannot provide IV or NG therapy and he cannot drink: refer him for IV therapy.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Identify treatment, Exercise B: treatments for Mai
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Identify treatment (2023)
narrative: In this exercise you will identify treatments for children who do not need urgent referral. Mai is 16-month-old, she has: No general danger signs FEVER- NO MALARIA (fever 38.5 °C; In clinic, ICT for malaria negative, fever present for 4 days), MEASLES WITH EYE COMPLICAIONS (pus draining from eye), NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION NO ANAEMIA. May has received BCG and 3 doses of (Penta ¸PCV and OPV) and 2 Rota doses.

questions.question: A. What treatments are needed for FEVER- NO MALARIA?
points: Give one dose of paracetamol in clinic for high fever (38.5°C or above).
Give appropriate antibiotic treatment for an identified bacterial cause of fever.
Advise the mother when to return immediately.
Follow-up in 3 days if fever persists.

questions.question: B. What treatments are needed for MEASLES WITH EYE COMPLICATIONS?
points: Give vitamin A treatment.
If pus draining from the eye, treat eye infection with tetracycline eye ointment.
Follow-up in 3 days.

questions.question: C. Look in the "Identify Treatment" column for NO ANAEMIA.
points: If child is less than 2 years old, assess the child's feeding and counsel the mother according to the feeding recommendations.
If feeding problem, follow-up in 5 days.

questions.question: D. Does May need a feeding assessment?
questions.explain: Yes, because she is less than 2 years old.

questions.question: E. What immunization does May need?
points: Measles immunization (and, by the schedule, the other 9-month vaccines: yellow fever and Men A).

questions.question: F. Should she be given vitamin (A) supplementation today?
questions.explain: Yes, she should receive vitamin A supplementation.

questions.question: G. What is earliest definite time for May to return for follow-up?
questions.explain: 3 days.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Identify treatment, Exercise C: when to return immediately
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Identify treatment (2023)
narrative: In this exercise you will describe when to return immediately for different cases. You will list the signs that you will teach the mother to watch for.

questions.question: 1. A child has: ● No general danger signs ● ACUTE EAR INFECTION ● NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION ● NO ANAEMIA What are the signs to return immediately?
points: Not able to drink or breastfeed
Becomes sicker
Develops a fever

questions.question: 2. A child has: No general danger signs Diarrhoea with NO DEHYDRATION PERSISTENT DIARRHOEA NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION NO ANAEMIA What are the signs to return immediately?
points: Not able to drink or breastfeed
Becomes sicker
Develops a fever
Blood in stool
Drinking poorly

questions.question: 3. A child has: No general danger signs COUGH OR COLD NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION NO ANAEMIA What are the signs to return immediately?
points: Not able to drink or breastfeed
Becomes sicker
Develops a fever
Fast breathing
Difficult breathing

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Identify treatment, Exercise D: urgent pre-referral treatments
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Identify treatment (2023)
narrative: In this exercise you will practice identifying urgent pre-referral treatments; Remember that these are in bold print on the ASSESS& CLASSIFY chart.

questions.question: 1. Nora is a 15-month-old girl. She has no general danger signs. She has: COUGH OR COLD, MASTOIDITS, NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION and NO ANAEMIA, and no other classifications. Nora needs urgent referral for MASTOIDITIS. Following is a list of treatments for all Nora’s classifications. Tick the urgent, pre-referral treatment(s): (Tick all that apply.)
options: a. soothe the throat and relieve cough with a safe remedy.
b. Advise the mother when to return immediately.
c. Follow-up in 5days if not better.
d. Give first dose of an appropriate antibiotic.
e. Give first dose of paracetamol for pain.
g. Assess the child’s feeding and counsel the mother on feeding. If feeding problem, follow-up in 5 days.
questions.explain: d, e and f. Soothing the throat is not urgent; the hospital will explain when to return and about follow-up; there is no time or need to assess feeding before referral.

questions.question: 2. Hanan is an 18-month-old girl. She has no general danger signs. She has NO SIGNS OF DEHYDRATION OR PERSISTENT DIARRHIEA, COMPLICATED SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRTION, NO ANAEMIA, and no other classifications. Hanan needs urgent referral for COMPLICATED SEVERE ACUTE MALNUTRTION Following is a list of treatments for all Hanan’s classifications. Tick the urgent, pre- referral treatment(s): (Tick all that apply.)
options: a) Give fluid and food to prevent dehydration (plan A).
b) Advise the mother when to return immediately.
c) Advise the mother on feeding a child who has persistent diarrhoea.
g) Treat to prevent low blood sugar.
questions.explain: e and f (the facilitator guide's answer), and g: treatment to prevent low blood sugar is one of the urgent treatments in this module's list. Plan A is not urgent and takes considerable time; the hospital will explain feeding, follow-up and when to return.

questions.question: 3. Omer is a 2-year-old boy. He is lethargic. has a fever of 39°C. The health worker classifies Omer as having VERY SEVERE FEBRILE DISEASE and CHRONIC EAR INFECTION. He has some palmar pallor so is classified as having ANAEMIA, although he is also classified as NO ACUTE MALNUTRTION Omer needs urgent referral for VERY SEVERE FEBRILE DISEASE. Following is a list of treatments for all Omer’s classifications. Tick the urgent, pre- referral treatment(s): (Tick all that apply.)
options: a) Give quinine for very severe febrile disease (first dose).
b) Give first dose of an appropriate antibiotic.
c) Treat the child to prevent low blood sugar.

PART 1:
1. a. What would you tell a mother about why it is important to treat an eye infection?
Treating an eye infection will prevent damage to the eye.
b. What major step of how to teach a mother to treat an eye infection is missing from the list
below?
Practice is missing.
* Explain how and why to treat the eye.
* Demonstrate how to clean the eye and apply tetracycline eye ointment.

anything else in the child's eye.

eye. Observe her as she practices and provide feedback.
* Give her one tube of eye ointment.
* Ask checking questions to make sure she understands the instructions.
c. Do you know how to treat your child's eye?
How will you treat your child's eye?
Can you hold your child still while you apply the ointment?
How, will you hold your child still so that you can put the ointment in his eye.
2. a. What would you tell a mother about why it is important to treat mouth ulcers?
It is important to treat mouth ulcers to control infection. Treating the child's mouth will
help the child eat normally sooner and get better faster.
2. b. What are the major steps you would follow when teaching a mother to treat mouth ulcers at
home?
∗ Explain the treatment for mouth ulcers. Explain why the treatment should be given.
∗ Describe the steps of the treatment (demonstrate if possible):
- Wash hands.
- Dip a clean cloth in salt water.
- Clean the mouth with the cloth.
- Paint the mouth ulcers with half-strength gentian violet. Use a clean
cloth or cotton-tipped stick, Wash the hands again.
∗ Ask the mother to practice cleaning her child's mouth and painting it with
gentian violet. Observe her while she practices.
∗ Tell the mother how often to give the treatment at home. Tell her to apply the
gentian violet for 5 days and then stop.
∗ Give the mother the bottle of half strength gentian violet (0.25%). For
example, if 0. 5 % gentian violet is available in clinic, dilute this with an
equal amount of water.
∗ Ask checking questions to make sure the mother understands how to treat
mouth ulcers.
c. List 3 checking questions you could ask to make sure the mother understands how
to treat mouth ulcers at home.
- How will you treat the mouth ulcers?
- What will you use when you treat the child's mouth ulcers?
- Why should you wash your hands?
- When will you wash your hands?
- How often will you treat the child's mouth ulcers?

A safe remedy is any remedy that does not contain harmful ingredients, such as tea with
honey or lemon.
b) Give at least 2 examples of remedies that are not safe.
Harmful remedies include medicated nose drops and those that contain atropine, codeine or
codeine derivative, or alcohol.

immediately for treatment?
- If not able to drink or breastfeed
- If becomes sicker
- If develops fever
- If fast breathing
- If difficult breathing

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Treat the child, Exercise Annex C-4: if you can only give Plan C by mouth
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Treat the child (2023)
narrative: Answer the questions about Saif, Eltayib, Hossam and Rashid.

questions.question: Write your answers to each question of the exercise. Then compare them with the answers.
points: TREAT THE CHILD Answers to Exercise Annex C-4
1. SAIF
a. Should you refer Saif urgently or try to rehydrate him by mouth?
Since Saif can drink some ORS solution, you should try to rehydrate him by mouth.
b. How much ORS solution should you give?
240 ml (20 ml x 12 kg) of ORS solution
c. Saif vomits frequently. What should you do?
Give the fluid more slowly
d. What should you do now?
Refer for IV treatment
2. ELTAYIB
a . How much ORS should the father encourage Eltayib to drink during the next hour?
300 mls(20 ml x 15 kg) of ORS solution during the next hour
b. What should the health worker do now?
The health worker should put Eltayib on- Plan B treatment. During the next 4 hours,
Eltayib should receive 900 - 1400 ml of ORS solution by mouth.
.c. For how long should the health worker encourage Eltayib and his father to remain
at the clinic? Why?
The health worker should encourage Eltayib and his father to remain at the clinic for
4 hours on Plan B and until closing time on Plan A. It is important that Eltayib and hi .father
remain for at least the Plan B treatment, to be sure Eltayib is rehydrated successfully. If
possible, they should stay 6 more hours to be sure that the signs of dehydration do not return.
3. HUSSAM
What should the health worker do?
Refer HUssam. The health worker should tell the grandmother to take Hussam to the
hospital urgently. The health worker should also help her figure out the fastest way to get
there.
4. RASHID
How should Rashid be treated?
Rashid should be referred urgently to the hospital because he has 2 severe classifications,
SEVERE PNEUMONIA OR VERY SEVERE DISEASE and SEVERE DEHYDRATION.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Treat the child, Exercise K: whether to immunize
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Treat the child (2023)
narrative: Decide which immunizations each child should be given today.

questions.question: Write your answers to each question of the exercise. Then compare them with the answers.
points: TREAT THE CHILD Possible Answers to Exercise K
1. Should Huaida be given the immunizations today?
Yes, Huaida should be immunized today. PNEUMONIA and MALARIA are
not contraindications to immunizations.
2. Should Kamal give the infant OPV 0 today?
No OPV0 is not given to an infant who is more than 14 days old.
3. a. Should the health worker give Rasha OPV 3 and Pentavalent3 today?
Yes. DYSENTERY is not a contraindication to immunizations.
b. What should the health worker tell the mother about possible side effects of OPV
and Pentavalent vaccines?
The health worker should tell the mother that there are no side effects of the OPV
vaccine, but sometimes there are side effects from pentavalent. Fever, irritability and
soreness are possible, but not serious. Fever means that the Pentavalent is working
Tell the mother to give paracetamol to Rasha if she feels very hot or is in pain.
c. How should the health worker record the immunizations?
The health worker should record the date that the Pentavalent is given on the
immunization card and in the clinic's register. The OPV 3 should not be recorded because
the child has diarrhoea today. Tell the mother to return in 4 weeks for another dose of
OPV 3 and IPV. When she returns, the health worker should then record the date of the
second dose.

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Counsel the mother, Exercise C: feeding problems and relevant advice
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Counsel the mother (2023)
narrative: For each written case, list the feeding problems and the relevant advice.

questions.question: Write your answers to each question of the exercise. Then compare them with the answers.
points: Answers to Exercise C
1. Feeding problem (s):
Not breast feeding often enough
Taking other milk (cow's milk 2 times per day)
Using feeding bottle
Correct Feeding Practices:
Breastfeeding day and night
Feeding the same during illness as in health
Relevant Advice:
You can produce all the breastmilk your child needs. Your child will gain weight better on
more breast milk than on cow's milk.
Give more frequent, longer breastfeeds, day and night, and gradually reduce amount of cow's
milk given. (If the mother will not increase breastfeeding to replace other milk, instruct the
mother to prepare cow's milk appropriately or change to another appropriate breast milk
substitute. To prepare cow's milk appropriately, mix ½ cup boiled whole cow's milk with ¼
cup water and 2 teaspoons sugar. Make sure that any breast milk substitute is correctly and
hygienically prepared and is used within an hour.)
Use a cup instead of a bottle.
Note: This mother will also need to be told to return for follow--up in 5 days since there
is a feeding problem.
2. Feeding Problem(s):
Child is receiving only 3 meals per day.
Family foods (rice and thin soup) are note varied and are not energy-rich.
Child is not fed actively. He shares a plate with siblings and does not get much food. Correct
Feeding Practices:
Giving family foods
Relevant Advice:
Feed the child 5 times each day.
Try to add some oil, vegetables, meat, fish, or other foods to the rice.
Give a thick food rather than thin soup.
Give other nutritious foods such as stiff porridge, thick and enriched porridge, and mashed
beans.
Save out an individual serving for the child and feed it to him, or help him get enough from the
shared plate. Feed him until he does not want any more.
Note: This child will need to be seen again in 5 days for feeding problems.
3. Feeding Problem (s): No situation in the exercise module
The child is being fed according to the recommendations for his age. However, the persistent
diarrhoea suggests that he is having trouble digesting cow's milk.
Relevant Advice..
Replace the cow's milk with yoghurt, OR replace half the cow's milk with nutritious foods such
as enriched porridge (thick porridge mixed with groundnuts and some oil added).
Note.. This child will need to be seen again in 5 day for follow-up for persistent diarrhoea.
4. Feeding Problem (s) -- Recorded on the front of the Sick Child Recording Form.
Complementary foods are not given often enough and are not thick and nutritious.
Mother has stopped cereal during illness.
On the back of the form, the participant should have written advice such as:
At this age the child needs more complementary foods.
Make porridge thicker and add oil and mashed vegetables or fruit.
Start now to give this 3 times daily, even during illness.
Also try combinations such as rice with vegetables, meat, or fish.
Keep breastfeeding as often as the child wants.
Follow up in 5 days.

questions.question: Write your answers to each question of the exercise. Then compare them with the answers.
points: Answers to Exercise C
1. a) How would you assess Haytham?
Completely assess Haytham as on the ASSESSS & CLASSIFY chart. Also, assess for other possible
causes of fever
b) How would you treat Haytham? If you would give a drug, specify the dose and schedule.
- If feasible, make a blood smear. If the blood smear is positive, treat with the second-line oral
antimalarial, DHAP, if available; if not refer to hospital.
- If blood smear is negative, refer to hospital.
- If blood smear is not feasible, give second-line antimalarial or, if not available, refer to
hospital.
- If the child is treated with second-line antimalarial, advise the mother to return again in 3
days, if the fever persists
- Give paracetamol (if fever is 38.5c)..
2. a) How would you treat Noon? If you would give drugs, specify the dose and schedule.
Since Sara has a general danger sign, treat her as for VERY SEVERE FEBRILE
DISEASE OR SEVERE MALARIA. Refer her urgently to hospital, but before referral give:
- Quinine -- 0.5 ml (300 mg/lml) plus 2.0 ml diluent, total 2.5mls
- Ampicillin (1 ml) and gentamicin (0.5 - 1 ml)
(since she cannot drink)
- Breastmilk, milk, or sugar water by NG tube if possible (since she cannot drink).
- Paracetamol can also be used by NGT

exercises.title: Sudan IMNCI: Follow-up, Exercise D: follow-up of the sick child
exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Follow-up (2023)
narrative: Answer the questions about the children who came back for follow-up.

questions.question: Write your answers to each question of the exercise. Then compare them with the answers.
points: Answers to Exercise D
1. a) Tick the items appropriate to do during this visit:
_√ _ Ask about any new problems. If yes, assess, classify and treat as at an initial visit.
_ √ _ Ask the questions in the top box of the COUNSEL chart. Identify any new feeding
problems.
_√ _ Ask the mother if she has been able to give John extra meals each day. Ask what she fed
him and the number of meals.
_ _ Since Mahmoud has not gained weight, immediately refer him to hospital.
_ _ Advise the mother to resume breastfeeding.
_ _ Give vitamin A.
_√ _ Since Mahmoud has had no weight gain, repeat the advice given to the mother before.
Behaviour change takes a long time.
_√ _ Ask the mother questions to identify additional feeding problems.
_√ _ Make recommendations for any feeding problems that you find.
_√ _ Ask if Mahmoud is still having diarrhoea.
b) What advice would you give Mahmoud 's mother now?
Talk to her about active feeding, such as: It is very good that you are giving him the ugali with
mashed beans as extra food. When you give him stiff porridge, sit with him for a few minutes
and encourage him to eat it. At family meals, give John his own plate of food, especially when
you serve meat, eggs, milk or avocado. It is very good that you are planning to get some eggs
and milk when you can afford to. They are very nutritious.
b) Should you ask the mother to bring Mahmoud back to see you? If so, when should she come
back? Why?
Yes. Since Mahmoud is very low weight for age, you want to be sure that he is gaining weight.
Since you are asking his mother to give different foods, to feed him more often and to sit with
John to encourage him to eat, you need to find out if she is able to feed John this way. You
would give her encouragement and reinforce some of the advice. She should come back in 30
days after the initial visit, that is, in about 3 weeks.
2. a) Write below 3 questions that you could ask Amal's mother to find out whether Amal's feeding
has improved.
• Describe for me how you are feeding Amal now. What do you give her for lunch and
for dinner?
• Does she eat the amount you serve her?
• When are you breastfeeding her?
• Have you been able to give her a mid-morning feed? What food do you give then?
b) What would you advise the mother today? Also write something to praise.
Soup is thin and does not give as much nutrition as the rice. It is better to give the mash of
beans-rice and oil first, and then give her some soup if she is still hungry. Serve her the
beans-rice first at both lunch and dinner.
It is very good that you are breastfeeding Amal in the morning now. It is also very good that
she is getting the mid-morning thick porridge. This food will help her grow.

exercises.source: Sudan IMNCI module: Follow-up (2023)
narrative: Answer the questions about the young infants who came back for follow-up.

questions.question: Write your answers to each question of the exercise. Then compare them with the answers.
points: Answers for Exercise E
1. a) How would you re-assess Sashie?
Look at the skin pustules. Decide if there are many or severe pustules. See if the redness
and pus of the pustules has improved.
b) What treatment does Sashie need now?
Tell the mother that Sashie's infection is improving, but that she must complete the 5 days of
antibiotic. She should also continue cleaning the skin and applying gentian violet on those
days.
2. a) How would you re-assess this infant?
Re-assess feeding as in the box "Then Check for Feeding Problem or Low Weight ". Ask
about the feeding problems found at the initial visit. Look for ulcers or white patches in the
mouth.
b) How will you treat this infant?
Praise the mother and encourage her to continue breastfeeding Afiya as she is now doing
well. Tell her that the thrush is improving. She should continue cleaning the mouth and
painting it with half strength gentian violet for a total of 5 days.
